'''Ángel Martín Municio''' ([[Haro, La Rioja|Haro]], [[La Rioja]], 30 November 1923 – [[Madrid]], 23 November 2002) was a Spanish scientist, researcher, and professor known for his contributions to [[physics]] and [[chemistry]].

== Biography ==
Municio earned degrees in chemistry and [[pharmacology]] from the [[University of Salamanca]] and the [[University of Santiago de Compostela]], respectively.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-19 |title=Ángel Martín Municio |url=https://www.rae.es/academico/angel-martin-municio |access-date=2025-05-08 |website=Real Academia Española |language=es}}</ref> He subsequently obtained [[doctorate]]s from the [[Complutense University of Madrid|University of Madrid]] (now the [[Complutense University of Madrid]]).

He was an assistant professor of [[organic chemistry]] at the Faculty of Sciences of the University of Madrid (1948–1951) and was later a collaborator and researcher at the [[Spanish National Research Council|CSIC]] and head of the biochemistry department of the Institute of Chemistry (1951–1967). He studied at various universities and institutions outside of Spain, such as the [[Utrecht University|Rijks Universiteit]] in [[Utrecht]] (1951–1954) and the [[Medical Research Council (United Kingdom)|Medical Research Council]] in [[Cambridge]] (1969).{{citation needed|date=May 2025}}

As a professor of [[biochemistry]] and [[molecular biology]] at the [[Complutense University of Madrid]] (1967–1989), he was the first Spanish individual to become a member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] in 1969. He represented Spain at the European Conference on [[Molecular biology|Molecular Biology]] between 1962 and 1990, and served as the vice-president from 1982 to 1990.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}}

He also served as vice-president of the European Language Resources Association, and as President of the [[Spanish Royal Academy of Sciences]]. He was the vice-director of the Spanish Royal Academy from 1992 to 1999, where he held the "o" seat as a member.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}}

He held other memberships and affiliations throughout his career, including: European Academies of Arts, Sciences and Humanities (1992); Scientiarum et Artium Europaea (1997);  Academies of Physical, Mathematical and Natural Sciences of Venezuela (1993); Sciences of Colombia (1994); [[Russian Academy of Sciences|Sciences of Russia]] (1996); honorary member of the Academies of Sciences of the [[Dominican Republic]] (1994); Spanish Language of Colombia (1997); and honorary member of the Interamerican Medical and Health Association (1993).{{citation needed|date=May 2025}}

He supervised several doctoral theses and was the author of numerous scientific publications and books.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}} 
[[File:D._Ángel_Martín_Municio_impartiendo_su_conferencia_"La_información_en_la_sociedad_celular"_en_la_Casa_de_las_Ciencias_del_Ayuntamiento_de_Logroño_1.jpg|thumb|300x300px|D. Ángel Martín Municio]]

== Honors and awards ==
He received various recognitions and awards, including: Medal of Merit for Research by the Royal Spanish Society of Physics and Chemistry; the [[Civil Order of Alfonso X, the Wise|Cross of Alfonso X the Wise]]; the Grand Cross of Military Merit; the Gold Medal of La Rioja; the Medal of Honor for the Promotion of Invention; the Medal of the Complutense University; and the Medal of Merit of the Government of Colombia.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}}

== Legacy ==
On February 18, 2010, a public square was dedicated close to his birthplace in [[Logroño]].{{citation needed|date=May 2025}}
